outcome: Given an access scenario spanning a facility, device, application, and data set, identify the subject, object, action, control plane, owner, and evidence needed to permit or deny the request.

sections.body: An access request is easier to govern when its subject, object, action, and context are explicit. A subject may be a person, device, process, or service; an object may be a file, record, facility, device, application, or network resource. Physical access controls movement through spaces and handling of tangible assets, while logical access controls information flows and system operations. Administrative controls set the rules, but a badge reader, operating system, application, or API must enforce them at the relevant boundary.
keyPoints: Physical and logical controls protect different manifestations of an asset and often must work together.
A username or badge is a claim or token; the policy still needs to decide what action is allowed.
Inventory, classification, ownership, and business need should precede control selection.
sections.title: Name the request precisely

sections.body: Centralized administration gives one function consistent policy and visibility; decentralized administration lets resource owners manage access close to the asset; a hybrid model combines central guardrails with delegated decisions. The choice is about accountability and operating context, not about whether enforcement is technical. A privileged administrator may need both a physical barrier and a logical control, with independent logs and periodic review so one compromised path does not silently bypass the other.
keyPoints: Centralized, decentralized, and hybrid describe administration and authority, not authentication factors.
Least privilege and need to know constrain what a permitted subject may do.
Access evidence should cover both entry to the environment and use of the resource.
sections.title: Choose where access is administered and enforced

sections.body: Apply the same request model—subject, asset, action, context, owner, policy, enforcement point, evidence, and revocation—to information, systems, devices, facilities, applications, and services. Information access may constrain reading, changing, printing, or exporting; systems and devices add administration, console, and physical-port paths; facilities add entry, escort, and visitor controls; applications and services add APIs, workloads, and service identities. Select identity assurance and least privilege proportionate to consequence, and preserve an accountable record. A common failure is protecting an application screen while leaving its data export, device administrator, physical facility, or service API path broadly available.
keyPoints: Make access decisions attributable to a subject, asset, action, context, owner, policy, enforcement point, and revocation path.
Test both expected allow behavior and abuse, failure, stale-access, or unavailable-dependency behavior.
sections.title: Authorize every physical and logical asset type

summary: Access control is the positive, reviewable control of subjects attempting to view, use, modify, move, or enter protected assets. A sound design coordinates administrative direction with physical and logical enforcement.

assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

options.feedback: Changed fact: A terminated contractor's badge is disabled, but the contractor's VPN certificate still works. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Treat the person, maintenance laptop, controller, lab, and update operation as separate subjects and objects. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Treat physical and logical deprovisioning as separate enforcement paths and revoke the certificate through the identity lifecycle process. Access is a set of paths, not a single account record.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implemented in 5 stable boundary states: Vendor technician requests escorted entry; valid login does not cross this boundary Restricted lab; Maintenance laptop connects only through approved maintenance path Monitored jump host. Its changed case is “A terminated contractor's badge is disabled, but the contractor's VPN certificate still works.” and every option returns to a named repair state.
